structures.name: Right Common Carotid Artery
structures.function: Supplies blood to the head and neck; divides into internal (brain) and external (face/scalp) carotid arteries
structures.location: Ascends within the carotid sheath alongside internal jugular vein and vagus nerve; bifurcates at C4 level (upper border of thyroid cartilage)
structures.bloodSupply: Branch of brachiocephalic trunk (right) / aortic arch (left)
structures.innervation: Carotid sinus: glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX); sympathetic plexus on artery wall
structures.clinicalNotes: Carotid pulse palpable at the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid at C4. Carotid endarterectomy for stenosis >70%. Carotid sinus massage may terminate SVT. Carotid body tumour (chemodectoma) at bifurcation.

structures.name: Right Internal Jugular Vein
structures.function: Drains blood from the brain, face, and neck; joins subclavian vein to form brachiocephalic vein
structures.location: Descends within the carotid sheath lateral to the common carotid artery; ends behind the sternal end of clavicle
structures.clinicalNotes: Preferred site for central venous catheter insertion. JVP (jugular venous pressure) reflects right atrial pressure. At risk during neck dissection and carotid endarterectomy. Thrombosis from IV drug use or Lemierre syndrome.

structures.name: Right Vagus Nerve
structures.function: Parasympathetic supply to thoracic and abdominal viscera; somatic motor to larynx and pharynx; visceral afferent
structures.location: Descends in carotid sheath between common carotid artery and internal jugular vein, posterior to both vessels
structures.clinicalNotes: Right recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under the right subclavian artery (shorter course than left). Injury causes ipsilateral vocal cord paralysis (hoarseness). Vagal syncope from carotid sinus stimulation.

structures.name: Facial Nerve
structures.function: Motor to muscles of facial expression; taste from anterior 2/3 tongue (via chorda tympani); parasympathetic to lacrimal, submandibular and sublingual glands
structures.location: Exits stylomastoid foramen, passes through parotid gland, divides into 5 branches (temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular, cervical)
structures.bloodSupply: Posterior auricular artery; branches of external carotid
structures.innervation: CN VII (self); chorda tympani carries taste and parasympathetic fibres
structures.clinicalNotes: Bell's palsy: idiopathic LMN facial nerve palsy (complete ipsilateral facial weakness including forehead). UMN lesion spares forehead (bilateral representation). At risk in parotid surgery and mastoidectomy. Ramsay Hunt syndrome: herpes zoster reactivation in geniculate ganglion.

structures.name: Hypoglossal Nerve
structures.function: Sole motor supply to all intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the tongue (except palatoglossus which is CN X)
structures.location: Exits hypoglossal canal, loops anteriorly around the occipital artery, passes deep to the posterior belly of digastric and stylohyoid, crosses the carotid arteries superficially
structures.clinicalNotes: LMN lesion: tongue deviates toward side of lesion (ipsilateral weakness). UMN lesion: tongue deviates away from lesion. At risk in carotid endarterectomy and submandibular gland surgery. Forms ansa cervicalis with C1-C3 fibres.

structures.name: Thyroid Gland
structures.function: Produces T3/T4 (metabolic regulation) and calcitonin (calcium homeostasis); bilobed with isthmus crossing trachea at rings 2-4
structures.location: Anterior and lateral to trachea and thyroid cartilage; two lobes connected by isthmus; pyramidal lobe may be present
structures.bloodSupply: Superior thyroid artery (from external carotid), inferior thyroid artery (from thyrocervical trunk); thyroid ima artery in 10%
structures.clinicalNotes: Recurrent laryngeal nerve runs in the tracheo-oesophageal groove posterior to thyroid lobe. Must be identified in thyroidectomy to avoid hoarseness/aphonia. Parathyroid glands lie posteriorly; inadvertent removal causes hypocalcaemia.

structures.name: Sternocleidomastoid
structures.function: Unilateral: ipsilateral lateral flexion + contralateral rotation of head. Bilateral: neck flexion and elevation of sternum in forced inspiration
structures.location: From manubrium (sternal head) and medial clavicle (clavicular head) to mastoid process of temporal bone and superior nuchal line
structures.bloodSupply: Occipital artery, superior thyroid artery, suprascapular artery
structures.innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) — motor; C2, C3 — proprioception
structures.clinicalNotes: Torticollis: fibrosis of SCM causing head tilt to affected side with contralateral rotation. Divides anterior triangle from posterior triangle of neck. Posterior triangle is bounded by SCM, trapezius, and clavicle.

structures.name: Brachial Plexus
structures.function: Provides all motor and sensory innervation to the upper limb; formed from ventral rami of C5-T1
structures.location: Roots emerge between scalenus anterior and medius; passes over the first rib and under the clavicle into the axilla; arranged as roots (C5-T1) → trunks → divisions → cords → branches
structures.bloodSupply: Vasa nervorum from subclavian artery branches
structures.clinicalNotes: Erb's palsy (C5-C6): waiter's tip deformity — arm internally rotated, extended, pronated. Klumpke's palsy (C8-T1): intrinsic hand muscle wasting + Horner's syndrome. Brachial plexus block for upper limb surgery. Pancoast tumour invades T1 root causing Horner's.

structures.name: Right Subclavian Artery
structures.function: Major blood supply to upper limb, posterior brain (via vertebral artery), and anterior thoracic wall (via internal thoracic artery)
structures.location: Arises from brachiocephalic trunk, arches over the first rib, passes between scalenus anterior and scalenus medius, becomes axillary artery at lateral border of first rib
structures.clinicalNotes: Subclavian steal syndrome: stenosis proximal to vertebral artery origin → retrograde vertebral flow → arm exercise causes vertebrobasilar symptoms. Scalene triangle formed between scalenus anterior, scalenus medius, and first rib (thoracic outlet).

structures.name: Trachea
structures.function: Conducts air between larynx and bronchi; cilia and mucus clear inhaled particles; C-shaped cartilage rings maintain patency
structures.location: Begins at C6 (inferior border of cricoid cartilage), descends in midline, bifurcates at T4-5 (carina) into left and right main bronchi
structures.innervation: Vagus nerve (CN X) and recurrent laryngeal nerve; sympathetic from middle cervical ganglion
structures.clinicalNotes: Right main bronchus is wider, shorter, and more vertical → foreign bodies more likely to enter right side. Tracheostomy usually performed between rings 2-4. Carina angle (subcarinal angle) widened by lymphadenopathy or left atrial enlargement.

structures.name: Accessory Nerve (CN XI)
structures.function: Motor to sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles
structures.location: Exits jugular foramen, crosses posterior triangle of neck superficially (at risk for iatrogenic injury), enters trapezius
structures.innervation: CN XI (self); spinal portion from C1-C5
structures.clinicalNotes: Most commonly injured nerve in the posterior triangle during lymph node biopsy. Injury → inability to shrug shoulder (trapezius) and weakness of head rotation (SCM). Winging of scapula may occur with trapezius weakness.

structures.name: Parotid Gland
structures.function: Largest salivary gland; produces serous saliva containing amylase; secretes 25% of total daily saliva
structures.location: Occupies parotid space anterior to the ear; between ramus of mandible anteriorly, mastoid process posteriorly, and zygoma superiorly; Stensen's duct opens into oral vestibule opposite upper second molar
structures.bloodSupply: Posterior auricular artery, superficial temporal artery
structures.innervation: Parasympathetic: glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) via tympanic branch, lesser petrosal nerve, auriculotemporal nerve. Sympathetic: superior cervical ganglion
structures.clinicalNotes: Facial nerve divides the parotid into superficial and deep lobes — superficial parotidectomy must preserve facial nerve. Parotid tumours: 80% pleomorphic adenoma (benign), 20% malignant (commonest: mucoepidermoid). Frey's syndrome post-parotidectomy: gustatory sweating.
